notes:
Sales/POC notes and SLO alignment log:

- Account background: Hypatia Reserve Labs — trading/market-risk org planning to move model inference for real-time trade surveillance and chat-based analyst assistants to a vendor-managed dedicated cluster. Very cost-sensitive but cannot compromise on 99th percentile latency for alerting pipeline.

- Primary ask: deterministic throughput guarantees and clear latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) for both streaming and non-streaming endpoints. Wants reserved GPU count + burst policy.

- Key contacts: CTO (R. Alvarez), Head of Platform (L. Osei), Security lead (K. Park). Red flags: strict data residency, audit trail, procurement wants 3 references.

- Timeline:
  * 2026-02-18: Intro + scoping (Fireflies ff_20260218_01_hypatia_kickoff) — defined workload mix: 60% real-time chat (avg 120 tokens), 30% reranking (short prompts, 1-3 candidates), 10% batch embeddings nightly.
  * 2026-02-25: Security questionnaire submitted (SEC-4042) — awaiting SOC2 Type II artifacts.
  * 2026-03-03: Technical deep-dive with SE (Samir) — agreed POC objectives and measurement plan (ff_20260303_02_perf-sync).
  * 2026-03-08: POC infra build started — provisioning dedicated GPU pool in partner region (private VPC).

- POC / SLO measurement proposal (current working doc: drive:/Hypatia/Redwood/latency-slo-spec-annotated.xlsx):
  * Measurement surfaces: define two canonical measurement surfaces — server_ingress (Redwood API ingress timing, excluding client network) and end_to_end_client (client SDK timing measured in Hypatia app). Both must be collected; SLOs defined primarily on server_ingress for SLA and end_to_end_client for product UX alignment.
  * Percentiles: p50/p95/p99 required for each surface. Proposed thresholds for non-streaming (chat responses returned as single response): p50 < 60ms, p95 < 180ms, p99 < 400ms for 256-token median workload. For reranking endpoints (short responses): p50 < 30ms, p95 < 100ms, p99 < 250ms. These are target, subject to validation during 72-hour POC run.

- Streaming vs non-streaming specifics: 
  * Streaming measurement split: first_byte_latency (time to first token) + per_chunk_tail (95th/99th per-token/chunk). Hypatia requires first_byte p95 < 150ms and per-chunk p95 < 80ms for 32-token chunks. Alerting is based on first_byte breaches for user interactivity; per-chunk variance used for quality regression detection.
  * Non-streaming (sync) responses measured end-to-end on server_ingress. Client-side telemetry will correlate network time; we recommend adding trace_id header in POC so logs can be joined.

- Instrumentation & reporting:
  * Redwood to expose server_ingress percentiles per model/route hourly and raw traces for sampled requests.
  * Hypatia will run client-side synthetic agents from 6 regions to capture network variance; compare client median vs server p95 to estimate network tail.
  * Agreed: use rolling 1h and 24h windows for SLO evaluation; weekly digest and immediate pager (pager duty) if 1h breach > 0.5% of requests.

- Reserved GPU planning (POC assumptions):
  * Target throughput target: 120 rps steady-state for chat (120 tokens avg), 400 rps for reranking short queries.
  * Initial reserved pool proposed: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs with 20% headroom and configurable burst to shared capacity. Redwood to provide kernel-level perf numbers and expected qps per GPU for chosen model (open-model v2-34B quantized) before perf run.

- SLA negotiation notes (legal):
  * Hypatia requests explicit latency SLA for p95 on server_ingress with credits tied to monthly breaches. Procurement prefers per-incident credits capped at 10% of monthly bill. Legal flagged unlimited credits as non-starter.
  * Need to draft clause for measurement surface (server_ingress) and tie to instrumentation (trace header + hourly metrics).

- POC success criteria (agreed):
  * Demonstrate sustained P95 below target for 72h on server_ingress for chat and reranking workloads with reserved pool and autoscale behaviors.
  * Show predictable tail behaviour for streaming first-byte latencies.
  * SOC2 docs provided to security team and procurement reference call completed.

- Next steps (short):
  * Run 72-hour perf window starting 2026-03-15 (ops: confirm GPU pool + dataset).
  * SE/SRE to publish per-route server_ingress percentile dashboards and sample traces.
  * Legal to exchange SLA redline draft by 2026-03-22.

- Quotes / paraphrases from call: 
  * "We need guarantees — if p99 slips during market open, our alerts misfire and we lose money." — Head of Platform (L. Osei).
  * "We can accept small credits but SLA definition must be deterministic and measurable at your ingress point." — Procurement.

- Open questions for Redwood SE: 
  * How is streaming per-token latency computed when requests are batched? (Samir action: provide batching+KV-cache accounting doc.)
  * Can Redwood emit a traceable request id header that survives retries and fallback routing? (ops action)

- Misc: Jira INF-9821 created to track perf test anomalies during POC.
